 Judgment
Dated this the 22nd day of May, 2025 The petitioner states that he has taken a shop building from the 3rd respondent on oral lease and is running a hotel business, taking registration from FSSAI.
According to the petitioner, he is in possession of the shop building for more than nine months.
Respondents 2 and 3 are now trying to forcefully evict him.
They have even used JCB for demolishing the building.
Unless this Court interferes in the matter and orders police to extend effective protection to the life of the petitioner, the petitioner will be put to loss.

2. When this writ petition came up for admission, this Court passed an interim order on 25.10.2024,
whereunder police protection was granted to the petitioner and his family members.
Counsel entered appearance on behalf of respondents 2 and 3 and resisted the writ petition.
Respondents 2 and 3 submitted that they have not granted the shop room on lease to the petitioner.
There is no piece of paper to establish the same.
The contention of the petitioner before this Court is that he is in possession of the building as per an oral lease from the 3rd respondent.
In fact, in the petitioner's complaint before the police, the petitioner submitted that he was taken the building on lease from Mr. Tejus C.T.
That itself would show that the petitioner has committed fraud and is creating fraudulent documents.

As the petitioner is in illegal possession, the petitioner cannot seek police protection to perpetuate the illegality.
4. Respondents 2 and 3 further pointed out that the petitioner has approached the civil court for an injunction against illegal eviction by respondents 2 and 3 and 2025:

the civil court has Rahees vs Station House Officer on 22 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/61462116/
2 not so far granted any interim or final injunction in favour of the petitioner.

sentences.text: Facts being so, the petitioner is not entitled to any police protection order from this Court.

5. Heard.
6.
The fact remains that the petitioner is in possession of the building owned by the 2 nd respondent.
The petitioner has obtained an FSSAI licence to run a hotel in the premises.
The facts being so, when the petitioner's possession, whether legal or illegal, is not disputed, the petitioner can be evicted only as per the procedure established by law.
Respondents 2 and 3 cannot use physical force to evict the petitioner from the shop building.
In the circumstances, the writ petition is disposed of directing the 1st respondent to grant adequate protection to the life of the petitioner.
It is made clear that any 2025:KER:35216 observations made in this judgment shall not affect either party in any civil proceedings that may be resorted to by the parties.
